method.CPU_measurement: Owned native bridge and hosted Windows/runtime cgroups; startup excluded. Percent uses one core as 100%. JACK, fixture and observer excluded.
method.timing_population: Armed by first NOTE_ON, then retained through shutdown; startup/initial silence excluded. Quantiles are histogram upper bounds.
method.runner_native_configuration: Pins the native Python launcher leader on BOTH lanes. The Box64 lane still translates the x86 Linux runtime; runner=native is a supervision mode, not guest ISA.
method.same_settings: No editor; LANG=C.UTF-8, PROTON_USE_XALIA=0, WINEDLLOVERRIDES=uiautomationcore= on both. No affinity, buffer, governor, cooling or dynarec tuning.

source_observation.native_queue: native-vst3-proxy/backend/src/queued.rs:634 sleeps for 50 us when no work is queued.
source_observation.windows_audio: windows-factory-probe/source/delivery_mailbox.h:19,49 polls with NtDelayExecution requesting 50 us; live setup measured about 104-107 us.
source_observation.windows_owner: windows-factory-probe/source/offline_processing.cpp:238 requests 50 us sleep between owner services; live setup measured about 1.06 ms for that sleep mechanism.
source_observation.source_check: The two Windows source files above are unchanged between the reused Windows artifact source commit and the current experiment head.
source_observation.interpretation: Frequent timer polling is a concrete candidate for fixed bridge overhead. No sampled CPU stack profile was collected; this is not a measured attribution of every CPU cycle or Pigments failures.

limits: Two 30-second runs per complete runtime stack, using a light source-owned synth; not a saturation benchmark.
Runtime, Wine and launcher versions differ; effects cannot be assigned solely to FEX versus Box64.
Governor remained ondemand. Samples were 1.6 or 2.4 GHz; short sampling does not characterize all frequency changes.
ABBA order counterbalances some drift; start temperatures differed, so there is no thermal-efficiency or sustained-temperature claim.
No Pigments, editor, preset/state recall, ShieldXL mapping or reduced-buffer qualification.
No new runtime or bridge build was needed for this comparison.
